messages:
maria: Quick RFC follow-up — proposing we split dashboard queries into two lanes: hot-cache path (edge precomputed tiles) and cold query path (full query-service). Main decision: where to perform RBAC? edge proxy vs query-service. TL;DR: edge = lower latency for cached hits but duplicate/partial checks; service = single source of thought but higher p95 for cold requests.

sam: Can you share numbers? rough p50/p95 impact?

maria: Sure. rough figures from bench: cached tile fetch ~18ms from CDN -> total ~28ms end-to-end. If we add authz at service for every request, cold auth adds ~12–20ms on the hot path (depending on DB lookups). So edge auth saves ~10–15ms on cache hits. Cold path will still do full checks; expected p95 around 220–280ms today.

anika: sounds reasonable. Would prefer hybrid: coarse-grained RBAC at edge (tenant+role check) and fine-grained checks in query-service when we execute sensitive projections. That keeps hot path fast and avoids obvious stale-allow cases.

lee: How do we keep cache correctness? If edge does coarse checks, we still need to invalidate when perms change. What's TTL strategy?

maria: Plan is short-lived permission tokens for edge, issued by auth service with TTL ~30s and revocation sequence. Edge caches tiles keyed by (tile-id, perm-token-v2). If token changes, cache miss forces cold path. Example header we plan to pass:

```
GET /tiles/abcd1234
Authorization: Bearer <session>
X-Perm-Token: perm_v2:eyJ...;seq=124
```

sam: Signed perm tokens + seq number looks ok. Concern: any chance of token replay or amplification? also cost of signing at scale.

anika: We can use HMAC-signed tokens from auth service; verification is O(1) CPU and avoids DB roundtrip at edge. Sequence number lets us forcibly bump tokens on role change.

lee: Who issues tokens? auth-service or query-service? If auth-service issues, edge only verifies HMAC. If query-service issues, edge becomes a dumb proxy. I think auth-service -> edge verify, query-service re-checks if request is cold.

maria: exactly. Edge verifies HMAC + seq and allows quick hits. Cold path always re-evaluates using current permission store (single source).

sam: CPU/cost note: duplicating checks means every cached hit still pays for HMAC verify at edge (small) + full check sometimes. Need to quantify — estimate ~0.3ms of CPU per verify at edge plus memory bandwidth. At 10k qps that's non-trivial.

anika: We can mitigate by using a tiny verification library in the edge binary (rust) that verifies HMAC from local key ring; also batch revalidation for bursts.

maria: Rollout idea: phase 0 — instrument and measure current tile hit p95; phase 1 — deploy HMAC token issuance and edge verify in canary (5% traffic) with metrics: auth-latency, tile-hit-rate-by-token, stale-rejects, 401 spikes; phase 2 — enable coarse-edge checks for 25% then 100%; phase 3 — enable optional fine-grained service checks as circuit breakers for suspicious flows.

lee: How will we test multi-tenant isolation? Need a chaos test that flips permissions and asserts that edge cache invalidates quickly.

maria: Agreed — add a small e2e harness: flip perm -> assert subsequent requests for affected tiles go cold within <TTL*2. Add synthetic load to ensure no latency regressions.

sam: What about metrics and tracing? We'll need a clear tag: lane=hot|cold, auth=edge|service, perm_seq, cache_key. Without that rollouts are blind.

maria: yep. I added the following to the console tracing spec:
- tags: lane, auth_check_location, perm_seq, tile_id, tenant_id
- counters: tile_fetch_total, tile_fetch_cache_hit, tile_fetch_auth_fail
- histograms: edge_verify_ms, service_auth_ms, end_to_end_ms

anika: Can we add an alert on sudden drop in hit-rate or spike in auth_fail? e.g., if cache-hit-rate drops >10% in 5m during rollout, auto rollback.

maria: Good call. We'll wire a rollout policy that auto-rolls back at threshold metric deltas.

deploy-bot: deploy 2023-11-07T15:22:30Z canary: dashboard-edge-auth-v2 -> 5% (ok) :rocket:

lee: One more: shard ownership and consistent hashing for tile-store. If we route tokens into cache keys, we must ensure uniform distribution so one tenant with lots of perms doesn't hot-spot a node. Consider adding tenant sharding dimension and fallback eviction quotas.

sam: Also document the tradeoff table in the RFC follow-up: latency benefit, operations complexity, attack surface, cost delta. We need sign-off from security before canary.

maria: I'll draft a short RFC follow-up with measured numbers and an explicit rollout checklist (canary metrics, e2e tests, security sign-off). Aim to start canary next Tuesday. Anyone object?

anika: No objections from me. :+1:

sam: Fine by me, but please include cost estimate.

lee: LGTM, add chaos test to CI.

maria: Thanks — I'll post the follow-up doc and link here when ready.
